$$

where the surface $S$ is defined by $z={e}^{x-y}$ for $0\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le x.$" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the partial derivatives of the graph $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}{e}^{x-y}={e}^{x-y} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}{e}^{x-y}=-{e}^{x-y}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the equation $z=g(x,y)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y,g(x,y)) & =⟨\frac{1}{z},\,\frac{xy}{z},\,z⟩{|}_{z={e}^{x-y}} \\  & =⟨{e}^{-(x-y)},\,xy{e}^{-(x-y)},\,{e}^{x-y}⟩ \\  & =⟨{{{e}^{y-x}}_{⏟}}_{P},\,{{xy{e}^{y-x}}_{⏟}}_{Q},\,{{{e}^{x-y}}_{⏟}}_{R}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can evaluate our surface integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨\frac{1}{z},\,\frac{xy}{z},\,z⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-{e}^{y-x}\cdot {e}^{x-y}-(xy{e}^{y-x})\cdot (-{e}^{x-y})+{e}^{x-y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-1+xy+{e}^{x-y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}(-1+xy+{e}^{x-y})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[-y+\frac{x{y}^{2}}{2}-{e}^{x-y}]}_{y=0}^{y=x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-x+\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}-1+{e}^{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{8}-x+{e}^{x}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{8}-1+e)-1 \\  & =-\frac{19}{8}+e\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186198389 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186198031 :question/id #uuid "c69a0f41-5b8f-5fcd-b058-94df2d7984bc" :question/math-academy-id "e-12383"} :knowledge-point/id the surface $S$ defined by $z=-3x+2y$ for $0 \leq x \leq 2$ and $0 \leq y \leq 1.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $\mathbf F$ through $S$ can be expressed as
![](images/c6/c682f99e66e12fb124beaee9ae090978444e402b74ce675f0eb2f7939c1ed06d.svg)
What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \left\langle u,\: v,\: -3u+2v \right\rangle
$$

over the domain 

$$
D = \big\{ (u,v) \: : \: 0 \leq u \leq 2, \: 0 \leq v \leq 1 \big\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(-3u+2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-3⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(-3u+2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\,-2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ into $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z+2y,\,3y+z,\,x-z⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=-3u+2v} \\  & =⟨(-3u+2v)+2v,\,3v+(-3u+2v),\,u-(-3u+2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨-3u+4v,\,-3u+5v,\,4u-2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨-3u+4v,\,-3u+5v,\,4u-2v⟩\cdot ⟨3,\,-2,\,1⟩ \\  & =(-3u+4v)\cdot (3)+(-3u+5v)\cdot (-2)+(4u-2v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-9u+12v+6u-10v+4u-2v \\  & =u\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z+2y,\,3y+z,\,x-z⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}u\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}u\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the missing expression is ${\color{blue}u}.$"} {:db/id 17592186533081} {:db/id 17592186198593 :question/id #uuid "412e405b-c9a9-5a1c-8e85-45f26189dce3" :question/math-academy-id "q-160887" 3.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{-2}^{3}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u+v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 4,\,-2\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u+v} \\  & =⟨u+v-v,\,2v-(u+v),\,uv⟩ \\  & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =u\cdot (-1)+(v-u)\cdot (-1)+uv\cdot 1 \\  & =-u-v+u+uv \\  & =uv-v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(uv-v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{-2}^{3}uv-v\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186198610 :question/id #uuid "a3bcb9d3-050c-5ab9-bd2a-436465223147" :question/math-academy-id "q-161360" :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "f754a120-8886-56d3-b535-398f13b91c9f" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}" :db/id 17592186398529} {:answer/id #uuid "d28df103-ae23-5647-a506-1bc60c332868" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{u}^{2}+uv+{v}^{2}" :db/id 17592186398530} {:answer/id #uuid "e85142cb-e059-512c-8b7b-18eee7a8c253" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2uv" :db/id 17592186398531} {:answer/id #uuid "e433762d-59a0-5efb-bef2-7687d8583f2a" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}" :db/id 17592186398532} {:answer/id #uuid "3a53a3c7-e2f5-50e9-afd4-d3b986017cf4" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2(u+v)^{2}" :db/id 17592186398533}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186398531} :answer-field/id #uuid "185487e5-090f-5815-93b2-dfc0c983e691" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186398528}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/problem "Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨{x}^{2},\,{y}^{2},\,{z}^{2}⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=x+y$ for $0\le x\le 2$ and $0\le y\le 2.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨{x}^{2},\,{y}^{2},\,{z}^{2}⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u+v} \\  & =⟨{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,(u+v)^{2}⟩\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,(u+v)^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & ={u}^{2}\cdot (-1)+{v}^{2}\cdot (-1)+(u+v)^{2}\cdot 1 \\  & =-{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}+{u}^{2}+2uv+{v}^{2} \\  & =2uv.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$"} {:db/id 17592186278495 :question/id #uuid "0bf481ef-95d3-5b3f-b324-29ecd57febda" :question/math-academy-id "q-161358" :knowledge-point/_questions [{:db/id 17592186198389 :knowledge-point/id #uuid "a3486150-b3c2-5faf-99d5-b42ced350996" :knowledge-point/title "Expressing Flux Over a Surface as a Repeated Integral"}] :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "10279bac-75c2-5820-bf33-84359cbf720e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "-7u+4v" :db/id 17592186275617} {:answer/id #uuid "397e53f3-63a0-518a-999e-8c3d8631bb27" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "4u+7v" :db/id 17592186275987} {:answer/id #uuid "897e0260-ef83-5fe5-9ee2-95ed9d4cd1a6" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "7u+8v" :db/id 17592186276718} {:answer/id #uuid "bd3f2f9b-ef08-5972-b94d-02717ccd84df" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "8u-7v" :db/id 17592186277162} {:answer/id #uuid "ee6d4a87-66ae-58b1-806a-631ade59590d" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "-7u-8v" :db/id 17592186277571}] :answer-field/correct {:answer/id #uuid "10279bac-75c2-5820-bf33-84359cbf720e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498 :db/ident :answer.type/math} :answer/value "-7u+4v" :db/id 17592186275617} :answer-field/id #uuid "8692e3d1-c9bd-5cca-9274-6af9e13d6963" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493 :db/ident :answer-field.type/radio} :db/id 17592186277965}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485 :db/ident :question.difficulty/easy} :question/problem "Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z,\,-y,\,2x⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=3x-2y$ for $0\le x\le 5$ and $-3\le y\le 3.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,3u-2v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 5,\,-3\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(3u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,3⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(3u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,\,2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z,\,-y,\,2x⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=3u-2v} \\  & =⟨3u-2v,\,-v,\,2u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨3u-2v,\,-v,\,2u⟩\cdot ⟨-3,\,2,\,1⟩ \\  & =(3u-2v)\cdot (-3)+(-v)\cdot (2)+2u\cdot 1 \\  & =-9u+6v-2v+2u \\  & =-7u+4v.\end{aligned}

$$

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,2u-2v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,-1\le v\le 2\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨x+y,\,2x-y,\,x+z⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=2u-2v} \\  & =⟨u+v,\,2u-v,\,u+(2u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨u+v,\,2u-v,\,3u-2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨u+v,\,2u-v,\,3u-2v⟩\cdot ⟨-2,\,2,\,1⟩ \\  & =(u+v)\cdot (-2)+(2u-v)\cdot (2)+(3u-2v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-2u-2v+4u-2v+3u-2v \\  & =5u-6v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨x+y,\,2x-y,\,x+z⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5u-6v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}(5u-6v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186398521 :question/id #uuid "d5e1155b-c484-5f31-a815-946d2d63d6df" :question/math-academy-id "q-161359" :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "c8c22e69-9068-5d72-8593-ce78861036f9" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{u}^{2}-uv+{v}^{2}" :db/id 17592186398523} {:answer/id #uuid "2f4db3f6-9c97-526b-8cb2-065c8f5de466" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}" :db/id 17592186398524} {:answer/id #uuid "7b2e8a80-65c9-5d70-9b0e-0e801e7e718d" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "(u+v)^{2}" :db/id 17592186398525} {:answer/id #uuid "9f182d4d-0129-52ff-90b2-56e5acb487b3" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "(u-v)^{2}" :db/id 17592186398526} {:answer/id #uuid "c1e4fd3a-37bb-5bcd-85c6-185c9a1d61c2" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{u}^{2}+uv-{v}^{2}" :db/id 17592186398527}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186398523} :answer-field/id #uuid "396da9a4-de3b-5bd7-8b5e-dfc780e10bb9" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186398522}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/problem "Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨zy,\,xz,\,xy⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=x-y$ for $-1\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le 1.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u-v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨zy,\,xz,\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u-v} \\  & =⟨(u-v)v,\,(u-v)u,\,uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨(u-v)v,\,(u-v)u,\,uv⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =(u-v)v\cdot (-1)+(u-v)u\cdot (1)+uv\cdot 1 \\  & =-uv+{v}^{2}+{u}^{2}-uv+uv \\  & ={u}^{2}-uv+{v}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨zy,\,xz,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}({u}^{2}-uv+{v}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}({u}^{2}-uv+{v}^{2})\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186423120 :question/id #uuid "29805411-7a4c-51f7-893d-a0f3dc3cef10" :question/math-academy-id "q-161377"} {:db/id 17592186423123 :question/id #uuid Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,v-u⟩

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,-3\le v\le 0\}.

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=v-u} \\  & =⟨(u+v)^{2},\,(u-v)^{2},\,uv⟩\end{aligned}

Integral Using a Formula"}] :question/problem "For a surface $S$ given by $y = h(x,z)$ for $(x,z) \in D,$ the flux of the vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D 
\Bigg( 
\bbox[3pt, border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}} \dfrac{\partial h}{\partial x} 
+ Q 
- \bbox[3pt, border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}} \dfrac{\partial h}{\partial z}
\Bigg) \: \textrm{d}A,
$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?

*Hint: The orientation of $S$ should be chosen such that the unit normal vector has a positive  $\mathbf j$-component.*" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

Since our surface $S$ is of the form $y = h(x,z),$ it can be parameterized as

$$
\mathbf{r}(x,z) = \left\langle x, \: h(x,z),\: z \right\rangle.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨1,\,\frac{∂h}{∂x},\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{z}^{′} & =⟨0,\frac{∂h}{∂z},\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{z}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & \frac{∂h}{∂x} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{∂h}{∂z} & 1\end{aligned}|=⟨\frac{∂h}{∂x},\,-1,\,\frac{∂h}{∂z}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

However, notice that the $\mathbf j$-component is negative. Therefore, we select the normal vector that points in the *opposite* direction:

$$
\mathbf{r}'_z \times \mathbf{r}'_x = - \mathbf{r}'_x \times \mathbf{r}'_z =   \left \langle -\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial x}, \: 1, \: -\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial z} \right \rangle
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,z))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{z}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{∂h}{∂x},\,1,\,-\frac{∂h}{∂z}⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂h}{∂x}+Q-R\frac{∂h}{∂z})\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186049883} {:db/id 17592186198602 :question/id #uuid "9923f940-6e67-51d8-8336-d46f1ce02fd1" :question/math-academy-id "q-161166" :knowledge-point/_questions [{:db/id 17592186198392 :knowledge-point/id #uuid "55cd2fdb-4cae-5f0b-bea0-e845d51190e1" :knowledge-point/title "Expressing Flux Over a Surface as a Repeated Integral Using a Formula"}] :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "0ae2d92e-ed1f-5f54-9f3e-4ce38b8da70d" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499 :db/ident :answer.type/text} :answer/value "$-P,\,$ $∂P,\,$ $∂x$" :db/id 17592186275570} {:answer/id #uuid "2786ad1c-2c77-5044-8bba-022ff896dea2" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499 :db/ident :answer.type/text} :answer/value "$P,\,$ $∂g,\,$ $∂x$" :db/id 17592186275839} {:answer/id #uuid "44ac2a5e-f444-5ab8-8d2f-b1befe6ae68f" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499 :db/ident :answer.type/text} :answer/value "$-P,\,$ $∂g,\,$ $∂x$" :db/id 17592186276081} {:answer/id #uuid "4e5bb47b-fd98-5623-8225-b6a60c57026d" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499 :db/ident :answer.type/text} :answer/value "$P,\,$ $∂g,\,$ $∂y$" :db/id 17592186276170} {:answer/id #uuid "8b5ef7c7-aca0-5aa4-b9ce-95d7314ff4ab" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499 :db/ident :answer.type/text} :answer/value "$-P,\,$ $∂g,\,$ $∂y$" :db/id 17592186276743}] :answer-field/correct {:answer/id #uuid "8b5ef7c7-aca0-5aa4-b9ce-95d7314ff4ab" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499 :db/ident :answer.type/text} :answer/value "$-P,\,$ $∂g,\,$ $∂y$" :db/id 17592186276743} :answer-field/id #uuid "62e5c477-cfc8-5f60-94c2-948eec13a409" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493 :db/ident :answer-field.type/radio} :db/id 17592186277901}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487 :db/ident :question.difficulty/moderate} :question/problem "For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

"4ec0f874-f1a4-5c03-8a41-bf094ee7ee97" :step/math-academy-id 44446 :step/next {:db/id 17592186199282}} {:db/id 17592186199300 :step/content {:db/id 17592186199470 :tutorial/content "Let's now derive a general formula for the flux through an *upward-oriented* Cartesian surface.

For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

Consider a surface $S$ given by the equation $z=g(x,y).$ The canonical parameterization of the surface is

$$
\mathbf{r}(x,y) = \left\langle x,\: y,\: g(x,y) \right\rangle.
$$

Computing the tangent vectors to the grid curves, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{∂g}{∂x}⟩ \\ {r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨0,\,1,\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & \frac{∂g}{∂x} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{∂g}{∂y}\end{aligned}|=⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the $\mathbf k$-component is positive, which indicates that our surface is upward-oriented.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,y))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

We summarize as follows:

- *For a surface $S$ given by $z = g(x,y)$ for $(x,y) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( -P\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial x} - Q\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial y} + R \right) \textrm{d}A.
$$

We have analogous results for surfaces of the form $y = h(x,z)$ and $x=k(y,z){:}$

- *For a surface $S$ given by $y = h(x,z)$ for $(x,z) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( -P\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial x} + Q - R\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial z} \right) \textrm{d}A,
$$

*where the unit normal to the surface is chosen such that the $\mathbf j$-component is positive.*

- *For a surface $S$ given $x = k(y,z)$ for $(y,z) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( P - Q\dfrac{\partial k}{\partial y} - R\dfrac{\partial k}{\partial z} \right) \textrm{d}A,
$$

*where the unit normal to the surface is chosen such that the $\mathbf i$-component is positive.*" :tutorial/id #uuid "d20203b0-e15f-5061-ae68-16676ec933dc" :tutorial/math-academy-id 7653 :tutorial/title "Formulas for Flux Over Cartesian Surfaces"} :step/id #uuid "299c6f48-c761-519a-8d96-161fea9d6df0" :step/math-academy-id 44449 :step/next {:db/id 17592186199299}} {:db/id 17592186199306 :step/content {:db/id 17592186199473 :tutorial/content "Let's calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
\mathbf{F}(x,y,z)=\left\langle (x-y)^2, \:(x+y)^2, \: 12xy \right\rangle
$$

 

through the surface $S$ defined by the Cartesian equation 

$$
z=2y-2x
$$

for $0 \leq x \leq 1$ and $0 \leq y \leq 1.$ 

For surfaces like this, substituting $x=u$ and $y=v,$ we obtain a parametrization 

$$
\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \left\langle u,\: v,\: 2v-2u \right\rangle
$$

over the domain 

$$
D = \big\{ (u,v) \: : \: 0 \leq u \leq 1, \: 0 \leq v \leq 1 \big\}.
$$

 

Recall that for a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2v-2u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2v-2u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,-2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ into $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨(x-y)^{2},\,(x+y)^{2},\,12xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=2v-2u} \\  & =⟨(u-v)^{2},\,(u+v)^{2},\,12uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨(u-v)^{2},\,(u+v)^{2},\,12uv⟩\cdot ⟨2,\,-2,\,1⟩ \\  & =(u-v)^{2}\cdot 2+(u+v)^{2}\cdot (-2)+12uv\cdot 1 \\  & =4uv.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux of $\mathbf F$ through $S$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨(x-y)^{2},\,(x+y)^{2},\,12xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}4uv\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}4uv\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2u\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{0}^{1}2v\,\text{d}v \\  & =[{u}^{2}]_{0}^{1}\cdot [{v}^{2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =({1}^{2}-{0}^{2})\cdot ({1}^{2}-{0}^{2}) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$" :tutorial/id #uuid "f32d6993-cd62-5fe7-98f3-9a89a815dbfc" :tutorial/math-academy-id 7666 :tutorial/title "Introduction"} :step/id #uuid "dd32837c-4771-57ff-abbc-360334e17eeb" :step/math-academy-id 44522 :step/next {:db/id 17592186199295}}] :activity/title "Calculating Flux Through Cartesian Surfaces" :activity/type {:db/id 17592186045463 :db/ident :activity.type/lesson} :db/id 17592186198485} {:db/id 17592186199306 :step/content {:db/id 17592186199473 :tutorial/content "Let's calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
\mathbf{F}(x,y,z)=\left\langle (x-y)^2, \:(x+y)^2, \: 12xy \right\rangle
$$

 

through the surface $S$ defined by the Cartesian equation 

$$
z=2y-2x
$$

for $0 \leq x \leq 1$ and $0 \leq y \leq 1.$ 

For surfaces like this, substituting $x=u$ and $y=v,$ we obtain a parametrization 

$$
\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \left\langle u,\: v,\: 2v-2u \right\rangle
$$

over the domain 

$$
D = \big\{ (u,v) \: : \: 0 \leq u \leq 1, \: 0 \leq v \leq 1 \big\}.
$$

 

Recall that for a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2v-2u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2v-2u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,-2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ into $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨(x-y)^{2},\,(x+y)^{2},\,12xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=2v-2u} \\  & =⟨(u-v)^{2},\,(u+v)^{2},\,12uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨(u-v)^{2},\,(u+v)^{2},\,12uv⟩\cdot ⟨2,\,-2,\,1⟩ \\  & =(u-v)^{2}\cdot 2+(u+v)^{2}\cdot (-2)+12uv\cdot 1 \\  & =4uv.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux of $\mathbf F$ through $S$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨(x-y)^{2},\,(x+y)^{2},\,12xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}4uv\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}4uv\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2u\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{0}^{1}2v\,\text{d}v \\  & =[{u}^{2}]_{0}^{1}\cdot [{v}^{2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =({1}^{2}-{0}^{2})\cdot ({1}^{2}-{0}^{2}) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$" :tutorial/id #uuid "f32d6993-cd62-5fe7-98f3-9a89a815dbfc" :tutorial/math-academy-id 7666 :tutorial/title "Introduction"} :step/id #uuid "dd32837c-4771-57ff-abbc-360334e17eeb" :step/math-academy-id {:db/id 17592186199300 :step/content {:db/id 17592186199470 :tutorial/content "Let's now derive a general formula for the flux through an *upward-oriented* Cartesian surface.

For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

Consider a surface $S$ given by the equation $z=g(x,y).$ The canonical parameterization of the surface is

$$
\mathbf{r}(x,y) = \left\langle x,\: y,\: g(x,y) \right\rangle.
$$

Computing the tangent vectors to the grid curves, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{∂g}{∂x}⟩ \\ {r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨0,\,1,\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & \frac{∂g}{∂x} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{∂g}{∂y}\end{aligned}|=⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the $\mathbf k$-component is positive, which indicates that our surface is upward-oriented.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,y))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

We summarize as follows:

- *For a surface $S$ given by $z = g(x,y)$ for $(x,y) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( -P\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial x} - Q\dfrac{\partial g}{\partial y} + R \right) \textrm{d}A.
$$

We have analogous results for surfaces of the form $y = h(x,z)$ and $x=k(y,z){:}$

- *For a surface $S$ given by $y = h(x,z)$ for $(x,z) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( -P\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial x} + Q - R\dfrac{\partial h}{\partial z} \right) \textrm{d}A,
$$

*where the unit normal to the surface is chosen such that the $\mathbf j$-component is positive.*

- *For a surface $S$ given $x = k(y,z)$ for $(y,z) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \left\langle P,\: Q,\: R \right\rangle$ over $S$ is given by*

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_D \left( P - Q\dfrac{\partial k}{\partial y} - R\dfrac{\partial k}{\partial z} \right) \textrm{d}A,
$$

*where the unit normal to the surface is chosen such that the $\mathbf i$-component is positive.*" :tutorial/id #uuid "d20203b0-e15f-5061-ae68-16676ec933dc" :tutorial/math-academy-id 7653 :tutorial/title "Formulas for Flux Over Cartesian Surfaces"} :step/id #uuid "299c6f48-c761-519a-8d96-161fea9d6df0" :step/math-academy-id 44449 :step/next {:db/id 17592186199299}} {:db/id 17592186199299 :step/content {:db/id 17592186198392 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186198034 :question/id #uuid "b81eb0cb-a740-5e86-921c-4baa8c179e55" :question/math-academy-id "e-12387"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "55cd2fdb-4cae-5f0b-bea0-e845d51190e1" :knowledge-point/key-prerequisites [{:db/id 17592186049883}] :knowledge-point/questions [{:db/id 17592186198602} {:db/id 17592186198605} {:db/id 17592186278512} {:db/id 17592186278515} {:db/id 17592186278516} {:db/id 17592186278519} {:db/id 17592186373979} {:db/id 17592186401240} {:db/id 17592186401247} {:db/id 17592186401254} {:db/id 17592186423121} {:db/id 17592186423122}] :knowledge-point/title "Expressing Flux Over a Surface as a Repeated Integral Using a Formula"} :step/id #uuid "4ec0f874-f1a4-5c03-8a41-bf094ee7ee97" :step/math-academy-id 44446 :step/next {:db/id 17592186199282}} {:db/id 17592186199470 :tutorial/content "Let's now derive a general formula for the flux through an *upward-oriented* Cartesian surface.

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u-v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$

$$

over the domain 

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨x,\,y-z,\,x+y⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u-2v} \\  & =⟨u,\,v-(u-2v),\,u+v⟩ \\  & =⟨u,\,3v-u,\,u+v⟩\end{aligned}

$$

$$

$$

x\le 1$ and $-1\le y\le 1.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{1}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u-2v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,-1\le v\le 1\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨x,\,y-z,\,x+y⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u-2v} \\  & =⟨u,\,v-(u-2v),\,u+v⟩ \\  & =⟨u,\,3v-u,\,u+v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨u,\,3v-u,\,u+v⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,2,\,1⟩ \\  & =u\cdot (-1)+(3v-u)\cdot 2+(u+v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-u+6v-2u+u+v \\  & =-2u+7v.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨x,\,y-z,\,x+y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-2u+7v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{1}(-2u+7v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$"} :step/id #uuid "709b1a46-4737-5277-9af4-5df159388f84"} {:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "10b5412c-a9ab-5d1e-8d26-9a4c8f27c8e6" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-2u+7v" What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,v-u⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,-1\le v\le 2\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z,\,y+2z,\,2x-y⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=v-u} \\  & =⟨v-u,\,v+2(v-u),\,2u-v⟩ \\  & =⟨v-u,\,3v-2u,\,2u-v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨v-u,\,3v-2u,\,2u-v⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =(v-u)\cdot 1+(3v-2u)\cdot (-1)+(2u-v)\cdot 1 \\  & =v-u-3v+2u+2u-v \\  & =3u-3v.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z,\,y+2z,\,2x-y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(3u-3v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}(3u-3v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$"} :step/id #uuid "01b09de2-5016-5421-a764-c1a1b5c31868" :step/next {:db/id 17592186499579}} {:db/id 17592186499570 :step/content {:db/id 17592186278495 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "10279bac-75c2-5820-bf33-84359cbf720e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-7u+4v" :db/id 17592186275617} {:answer/id #uuid "397e53f3-63a0-518a-999e-8c3d8631bb27" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "4u+7v" :db/id 17592186275987} {:answer/id #uuid "897e0260-ef83-5fe5-9ee2-95ed9d4cd1a6" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "7u+8v" :db/id 17592186276718} {:answer/id #uuid "bd3f2f9b-ef08-5972-b94d-02717ccd84df" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "8u-7v" :db/id 17592186277162} {:answer/id #uuid "ee6d4a87-66ae-58b1-806a-631ade59590d" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-7u-8v" :db/id 17592186277571}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186275617} :answer-field/id #uuid "8692e3d1-c9bd-5cca-9274-6af9e13d6963" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186277965}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/id #uuid "0bf481ef-95d3-5b3f-b324-29ecd57febda" :question/math-academy-id "q-161358" :question/problem "Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z,\,-y,\,2x⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=3x-2y$ for $0\le x\le 5$ and $-3\le y\le 3.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,3u-2v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 5,\,-3\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(3u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,3⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(3u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,\,2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z,\,-y,\,2x⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=3u-2v} \\  & =⟨3u-2v,\,-v,\,2u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨3u-2v,\,-v,\,2u⟩\cdot ⟨-3,\,2,\,1⟩ \\  & =(3u-2v)\cdot (-3)+(-v)\cdot (2)+2u\cdot 1 \\  & =-9u+6v-2v+2u \\  & =-7u+4v.\end{aligned}

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u+v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,0\le v\le 2\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨{x}^{2},\,{y}^{2},\,{z}^{2}⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u+v} \\  & =⟨{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,(u+v)^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,(u+v)^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & ={u}^{2}\cdot (-1)+{v}^{2}\cdot (-1)+(u+v)^{2}\cdot 1 \\  & =-{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}+{u}^{2}+2uv+{v}^{2} \\  & =2uv.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨{x}^{2},\,{y}^{2},\,{z}^{2}⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2uv)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}2uv\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$"} :step/id #uuid "4dda445a-4e0e-5224-bc48-e70c3bb8a968" :step/next {:db/id 17592186499621}} {:db/id 17592186499621 :step/content {:db/id 17592186278506 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "1522d126-bc34-5af8-9b6a-e28d9a69cc28" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "3" :db/id 17592186275676} {:answer/id #uuid "18a12e63-447a-54f3-aa1b-7655d054b2a6" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{3}{2}" :db/id 17592186275705} {:answer/id #uuid "7f0d9dd7-0a4c-53a0-93f3-266c540e5806" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{11}{6}" :db/id 17592186276630} {:answer/id #uuid "e0ec1fd9-ea87-51b3-9aac-bec86160b60b" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{5}{6}" :db/id 17592186277443} {:answer/id #uuid "eb954333-7f24-5dd3-958d-038c55f1b656" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2" :db/id 17592186277536}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186277536} :answer-field/id #uuid "e7b5f25c-b535-59ae-8da4-9392f8bb667d" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186278131}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "154ea74b-7c8a-5b64-880d-29244a657638" :question/math-academy-id "q-161382" :question/problem "Evaluate the surface integral

where the surface $S$ is defined by $z=2x+y$ for $0\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le 1.$" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the partial derivatives of the graph $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x+y)=2 \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x+y)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the equation $z=g(x,y)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y,g(x,y)) & =⟨-x,\,-y,\,xyz⟩{|}_{z=2x+y} \\  & =⟨-x,\,-y,\,xy(2x+y)⟩ \\  & =⟨{{-x}_{⏟}}_{P},\,{{-y}_{⏟}}_{Q},\,{{xy(2x+y)}_{⏟}}_{R}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can evaluate our surface integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨-x,\,-y,\,xyz⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-(-x)\cdot 2-(-y)\cdot (1)+xy(2x+y))\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2x+y+2{x}^{2}y+x{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2x+y+2{x}^{2}y+x{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[2xy+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}+{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+\frac{x{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(2x+\frac{1}{2}+{x}^{2}+\frac{x}{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}+\frac{7x}{3}+\frac{1}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+\frac{7{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{x}{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}+\frac{7}{6}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$"} :step/id #uuid "d9521b99-85a2-58ce-8fc3-398a930f1cb4" :step/next {:db/id 17592186499567}}] :activity/title "Calculating Flux Through Cartesian Surfaces" :activity/type {:db/id 17592186045464 :db/ident :activity.type/review} :db/id 17592186498727} {:db/id 17592186499570 :step/content {:db/id 17592186278495 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "10279bac-75c2-5820-bf33-84359cbf720e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-7u+4v" :db/id 17592186275617} {:answer/id #uuid "397e53f3-63a0-518a-999e-8c3d8631bb27" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "4u+7v" :db/id 17592186275987} {:answer/id #uuid "897e0260-ef83-5fe5-9ee2-95ed9d4cd1a6" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "7u+8v" :db/id 17592186276718} {:answer/id #uuid "bd3f2f9b-ef08-5972-b94d-02717ccd84df" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "8u-7v" :db/id 17592186277162} {:answer/id #uuid "ee6d4a87-66ae-58b1-806a-631ade59590d" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-7u-8v" :db/id 17592186277571}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186275617} :answer-field/id #uuid "8692e3d1-c9bd-5cca-9274-6af9e13d6963" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186277965}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/id #uuid "0bf481ef-95d3-5b3f-b324-29ecd57febda" :question/math-academy-id "q-161358" :question/problem "Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z,\,-y,\,2x⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=3x-2y$ for $0\le x\le 5$ and $-3\le y\le 3.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,3u-2v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 5,\,-3\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(3u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,3⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(3u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,\,2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z,\,-y,\,2x⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=3u-2v} \\  & =⟨3u-2v,\,-v,\,2u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨3u-2v,\,-v,\,2u⟩\cdot ⟨-3,\,2,\,1⟩ \\  & =(3u-2v)\cdot (-3)+(-v)\cdot (2)+2u\cdot 1 \\  & =-9u+6v-2v+2u \\  & =-7u+4v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z,\,-y,\,2x⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-7u+4v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{5}{\int }_{-3}^{3}(-7u+4v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$"} :step/id #uuid "085a5662-c83a-5261-aadd-4e17a1724de2" :step/next {:db/id 17592186499585}} {:db/id 17592186499567 :step/content {:db/id 17592186278518 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "002ddc9f-2c71-5478-8c1d-77a6a8c334bf" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "3u-3v" :db/id 17592186275480} {:answer/id #uuid "023841e2-2821-56a0-955a-89084c15f8d2" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2u+v" :db/id 17592186275496} {:answer/id #uuid "4d835b30-d2dd-53ba-9310-a5a2961e3b3e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "u+2v" :db/id 17592186276160} {:answer/id #uuid "b4df5cbd-8643-5942-bb9e-8d044eb77815" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2u-3v" :db/id 17592186277092} {:answer/id #uuid "f42daa7a-2c08-5500-aa68-d0405d0dc904" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "3v+u" :db/id 17592186277615}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186275480} :answer-field/id #uuid "ca208624-88d6-5a85-8572-2dd062347b32" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186278079}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/id #uuid "06f1e075-9f39-52f0-b9b8-c179d2533ffc" :question/math-academy-id "q-161462" :question/problem "Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z,\,y+2z,\,2x-y⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=y-x$ for $0\le x\le 2$ and $-1\le y\le 2.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,v-u⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,-1\le v\le 2\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z,\,y+2z,\,2x-y⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=v-u} \\  & =⟨v-u,\,v+2(v-u),\,2u-v⟩ \\  & =⟨v-u,\,3v-2u,\,2u-v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u+v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,0\le v\le 2\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨{x}^{2},\,{y}^{2},\,{z}^{2}⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u+v} \\  & =⟨{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,(u+v)^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨{u}^{2},\,{v}^{2},\,(u+v)^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & ={u}^{2}\cdot (-1)+{v}^{2}\cdot (-1)+(u+v)^{2}\cdot 1 \\  & =-{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}+{u}^{2}+2uv+{v}^{2} \\  & =2uv.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨{x}^{2},\,{y}^{2},\,{z}^{2}⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2uv)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}2uv\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$"} :step/id #uuid "4dda445a-4e0e-5224-bc48-e70c3bb8a968" :step/next {:db/id 17592186499621}} {:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "8ffab214-a531-5f16-9548-4aba64a14e09" :answer/type {:db/id $$

We first compute the partial derivatives of the graph $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x+y)=2 \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x+y)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the equation $z=g(x,y)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y,g(x,y)) & =⟨-x,\,-y,\,xyz⟩{|}_{z=2x+y} \\  & =⟨-x,\,-y,\,xy(2x+y)⟩ \\  & =⟨{{-x}_{⏟}}_{P},\,{{-y}_{⏟}}_{Q},\,{{xy(2x+y)}_{⏟}}_{R}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can evaluate our surface integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨-x,\,-y,\,xyz⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-(-x)\cdot 2-(-y)\cdot (1)+xy(2x+y))\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2x+y+2{x}^{2}y+x{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2x+y+2{x}^{2}y+x{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[2xy+\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}+{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+\frac{x{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(2x+\frac{1}{2}+{x}^{2}+\frac{x}{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}+\frac{7x}{3}+\frac{1}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+\frac{7{x}^{2}}{6}+\frac{x}{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}+\frac{7}{6}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}

Since our surface $S$ is of the form $z=g(x,y),$ it can be parameterized as

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{∂g}{∂x}⟩ \\ {r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨0,\,1,\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}⟩\end{aligned}

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u-3v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 2,\,-1\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,3,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨x+z,\,2z,\,y+z⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u-3v} \\  & =⟨u+u-3v,\,2(u-3v),\,v+u-3v⟩ \\  & =⟨2u-3v,\,2u-6v,\,u-2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨2u-3v,\,2u-6v,\,u-2v⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,3,\,1⟩ \\  & =(2u-3v)\cdot (-1)+(2u-6v)\cdot (3)+(u-2v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-2u+3v+6u-18v+u-2v \\  & =5u-17v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5u-17v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}(5u-17v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$"} :step/id #uuid "89beea92-c19b-5b20-850a-a15dc788a7e6" :step/next {:db/id 17592186539046}} {:db/id 17592186539078 :step/content {:db/id 17592186198593 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "1cea6d00-8d2b-5733-8616-9267687fd149" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "uv+v" :db/id 17592186423087} {:answer/id #uuid "63293960-e3b1-529e-96e9-642aedf596e5" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "uv-v" :db/id 17592186423095} {:answer/id #uuid "84b21f44-ef97-5299-8654-bb5534b15960" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{u}^{2}+uv+{v}^{2}" :db/id 17592186423098} {:answer/id #uuid "cb8fdbef-d72d-513a-8e44-4a96d82e4382" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2{u}^{2}v-uv+{v}^{2}" :db/id 17592186423108} {:answer/id #uuid "e83e93b0-2e8f-5324-b1ed-23d683ac8523" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "u+v" :db/id 17592186423110}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186423095} :answer-field/id #uuid "7ab05865-9935-59ef-90a4-5cba4fa4f3d9" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186194189}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/id #uuid "412e405b-c9a9-5a1c-8e85-45f26189dce3" :question/math-academy-id "q-160887" :question/problem "Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=x+y$ for $0\le x\le 4$ and $-2\le y\le 3.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u+v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 4,\,-2\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u+v} \\  & =⟨u+v-v,\,2v-(u+v),\,uv⟩ \\  & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =u\cdot (-1)+(v-u)\cdot (-1)+uv\cdot 1 \\  & =-u-v+u+uv \\  & =uv-v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(uv-v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{-2}^{3}uv-v\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$"} :step/id #uuid "8b341075-9f21-55e2-b6de-970ecf70e05a" :step/next {:db/id 17592186539083}} {:db/id 17592186539083 :step/content {:db/id 17592186423123 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "0b89c0b5-bd8b-5088-a053-0db9bc0fd31f" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-uv" :db/id 17592186423085} {:answer/id #uuid "57bc1e11-c92f-5bf5-b1cd-bdfca274f1c3" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "5uv" :db/id 17592186423091} {:answer/id #uuid "62a07ee3-0b12-5f4d-81e0-7183964e0136" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "3u{v}^{2}" :db/id 17592186423094} {:answer/id #uuid "876d48e1-3fb3-5bc6-88d3-a7e99ab5d29a" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "uv+v" :db/id 17592186423100} {:answer/id #uuid "b65ee624-a7db-5060-ba14-007644627aeb" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "uv-v" :db/id 17592186423104}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186423091} :answer-field/id #uuid "dce1231b-682c-5119-8b60-1e600b81511c" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186423118}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/id #uuid "92e8ddd2-ccb6-5c20-b74b-2f784e857a55" :question/math-academy-id "q-161379" :question/problem "Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=y-x$ for $-1\le x\le 1$ and $-3\le y\le 0.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,v-u⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,-3\le v\le 0\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=v-u} \\  & =⟨(u+v)^{2},\,(u-v)^{2},\,uv⟩\end{aligned}

$$

$$

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,2u-4v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-2\le u\le 0,\,-1\le v\le 5\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u-4v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u-4v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & -4\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,4,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z+x,\,y+2z,\,x-4y⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=2u-4v} \\  & =⟨2u-4v+u,\,v+2(2u-4v),\,u-4v⟩ \\  & =⟨3u-4v,\,4u-7v,\,u-4v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨3u-4v,\,4u-7v,\,u-4v⟩\cdot ⟨-2,\,4,\,1⟩ \\  & =(3u-4v)\cdot (-2)+(4u-7v)\cdot 4+(u-4v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-6u+8v+16u-28v+u-4v \\  & =11u-24v.\end{aligned}
$$

$$"} :step/id #uuid "bfcd2b83-a5f2-52eb-abff-126d7bb1b47b" :step/next {:db/id 17592186539074}}] :activity/title "Calculating Flux Through Cartesian Surfaces" :activity/type {:db/id 17592186045464 :db/ident :activity.type/review} :db/id 17592186538230} {:db/id 17592186539078 :step/content {:db/id 17592186198593 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "1cea6d00-8d2b-5733-8616-9267687fd149" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "uv+v" :db/id 17592186423087} {:answer/id #uuid "63293960-e3b1-529e-96e9-642aedf596e5" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "uv-v" :db/id 17592186423095} {:answer/id #uuid "84b21f44-ef97-5299-8654-bb5534b15960" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "{u}^{2}+uv+{v}^{2}" :db/id 17592186423098} {:answer/id #uuid "cb8fdbef-d72d-513a-8e44-4a96d82e4382" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2{u}^{2}v-uv+{v}^{2}" :db/id 17592186423108} {:answer/id #uuid "e83e93b0-2e8f-5324-b1ed-23d683ac8523" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "u+v" :db/id 17592186423110}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186423095} :answer-field/id #uuid "7ab05865-9935-59ef-90a4-5cba4fa4f3d9" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186194189}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/id #uuid "412e405b-c9a9-5a1c-8e85-45f26189dce3" :question/math-academy-id "q-160887" :question/problem "Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=x+y$ for $0\le x\le 4$ and $-2\le y\le 3.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{-2}^{3}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?" :question/worked-solution "For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u+v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 4,\,-2\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u+v} \\  & =⟨u+v-v,\,2v-(u+v),\,uv⟩ \\  & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =u\cdot (-1)+(v-u)\cdot (-1)+uv\cdot 1 \\  & =-u-v+u+uv \\  & =uv-v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(uv-v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{-2}^{3}uv-v\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$"} :step/id #uuid "8b341075-9f21-55e2-b6de-970ecf70e05a" :step/next {:db/id 17592186539083}} {:db/id 17592186539046 :step/content {:db/id 17592186423122 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "45ff11c7-5335-5ffb-9240-826266b3b1ec" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "$∂z,∂g,$ and $-1$" :db/id 17592186423089} {:answer/id #uuid "73c7f141-a638-5c2f-a226-4db1e183214c" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "$∂x,∂g,$ and $-R$" :db/id 17592186423097} {:answer/id #uuid "d23fc8da-8bb8-570e-94f8-2dd437e7348c" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "$∂x,∂g,$ and $1$" :db/id 17592186423109} {:answer/id #uuid "f0b4e080-429e-59c9-b7b0-c3e775d0e61a" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "$∂x,∂g,$ and $-1$" :db/id 17592186423111} {:answer/id #uuid "f2a31230-1787-5f1a-a9cf-ba9794a07b89" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "$∂x,∂g,$ and $R$" :db/id 17592186423114}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186423114} :answer-field/id #uuid "2a3936a3-b7fb-5980-bcc0-5a21e600fc1e" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186423115}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/id #uuid "5b08ff1d-1edf-523c-a8e8-287f135b6040" :question/math-academy-id "q-162607" :question/problem "For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by
